images.title: The top without building the pyramid
images.purpose: Shows the shortcut a + 2b + c on the bottom row 4, 13, 8: the middle box counts twice, so the top is 38.
images.composition: One three row pyramid in the centre with the middle row left empty, and the shortcut written beside it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Six square boxes stacked as a pyramid. Bottom row of three boxes holding 4, 13 and 8 from left to right; the boxes holding 4 and 8 have teal (#0072B2) outlines, the box holding 13 has an amber (#E69F00) outline with a small amber badge × 2 just below it. Middle row: two empty boxes with thin dashed grey (#6B7280) outlines. Top box with a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline holding 38. To the right of the pyramid, the expression a + 2b + c in dark text. Exactly 6 boxes, 2 of them empty and dashed; no arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The middle box counts twice, so the top is a + 2b + c.
images.description: Shows the shortcut a + 2b + c on the bottom row 4, 13, 8: the middle box counts twice, so the top is 38.

image_decisions.why: The practice is about predicting the top from the bottom row; one pyramid with the middle row skipped shows the shortcut the tool checks.
